D.t: Amy Klobuchar leads by 13.8 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 383,451 votes; a one point swing is about 13,944 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +6.6 and D +20.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +10.2. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +17.4; your worst is co/efficient (R) at D +5.9. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 306,882 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 130,835 votes; Dakota, a projected net 45,449 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +4.7, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +2.5, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +4.1, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +9.5, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Amy Klobuchar runs furthest behind in Carver, Stearns, Wright. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 53 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.99 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Amy Klobuchar: Immigration voters 20 to 77, Small counties 40 to 56, Incomes $125K and up 46 to 51. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$3.5M cash against $618K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points away from Amy Klobuchar. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $6.2M helping Lisa Demuth and $1.3M helping Amy Klobuchar.

R.t: Lisa Demuth trails by 13.8 and wins 1% of simulations. Closing it takes about 191,725 voters switching sides, or 383,451 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +20.7 and D +6.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +10.2. Your best recent poll is co/efficient (R) at D +5.9; your worst is New York Times/Siena at D +17.4. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Wright, a projected net 19,164 votes; Stearns, a projected net 18,065 votes; Sherburne, a projected net 13,403 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +4.7, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +2.5, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +4.1, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +9.5, 1.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lisa Demuth runs furthest behind in St. Louis, Chisago, Rice. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 44 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 42 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 37 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.99 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Lisa Demuth: Black voters 18 to 80, Asian and other voters 26 to 72, Corruption voters 28 to 69. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$618K cash against $3.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points toward Lisa Demuth. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
